title: Data Presentation: Tables, Bar Charts, Line Graphs and Pie Charts
seo_title: Data Presentation – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Collect and present data in tables, bar charts, line graphs and pie charts; read and interpret data from charts and tables. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on data presentation: reading tables and timetables, bar charts, line graphs and pie charts. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Read the title, the axes and the scale
key_sub: A pie chart shows parts of a whole.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A table puts data in rows and columns. A bar chart shows amounts with bars.
  • A line graph shows how something changes over time, such as temperature through a day.
  • A pie chart shows parts of a whole. The whole circle is 360°: half the circle is 180° and a quarter is 90°.

Examples

Example

A quarter of a pie chart of 40 pupils

40 ÷ 4

Answer: 10 pupils

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not reading the scaleEach line on the axis may stand for 2, 5 or 10.
Reading the wrong barUse a ruler across to the axis.
Forgetting the whole pie is 360°Use 360° to find the angle of each part.

faq.q: Which chart is best for change over time?
Which chart shows parts of a whole?

faq.a: Facts or numbers that we collect.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Thursday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Thu bar ends on the line for 4. So the answer is 4 cakes.

items.q: How many points did Hawk House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Hawk bar ends on the line for 35. So the answer is 35 points.

items.q: How many space books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Space bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25. So the answer is 25 books.

items.q: How many pupils have a hamster?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Hamster bar ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 20 cans?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 20 on the scale. The 3C bar ends on the line for 20.

items.q: How many pupils cycle to school?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Bike bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 pupils.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which bar shows the most minibeasts?
items.e: The Woodlouse bar is the tallest one. The Woodlouse bar ends on the line for 14. It shows 14 minibeasts.

items.q: How many votes did Pear get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Pear bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25. So the answer is 25 votes.

items.q: How many pupils chose cricket?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Cricket bar ends on the line for 20. So the answer is 20 pupils.

items.q: How many votes did Blue get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blue bar ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. So the answer is 11 votes.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest lollies?
items.e: The Orange bar is the shortest one. The Orange bar ends on the line for 20. It shows 20 lollies.

items.q: How many books did Ikenna read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Ikenna bar ends on the line for 15. So the answer is 15 books.

items.q: How many stickers has Chiamaka got?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Chiamaka bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 stickers.

items.q: Which bar shows 15 lollies?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 15 on the scale. The Orange bar ends halfway between 10 and 20, so it shows 15.

items.q: How many space books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Space bar ends on the line for 50. So the answer is 50 books.

items.q: Which bar shows the most books?
items.e: The Temi bar is the tallest one. The Temi bar ends on the line for 30. It shows 30 books.

items.q: How many blackbirds were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blackbird bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 birds.

items.q: Which bar shows 8 cakes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 8 on the scale. The Fri bar ends on the line for 8.

items.q: On the temperature scale, what is each small square worth?
items.e: The labels go 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 5 small squares between two labels. 5 ÷ 5 = 1, so each small square is 1 °C.

items.q: What was the temperature at 10:00?
items.e: Go up from 10:00 to the point, then across to the scale. It is 1 small square above 10, so 11 °C.

items.q: What was the highest temperature?
items.e: The highest point is at 14:00. It is 3 small squares above 15, so 18 °C. (20 °C is the top of the scale, not a reading.)

items.q: What was the lowest temperature?
items.e: The lowest point is at 06:00. It is 4 small squares above 0, so 4 °C. (6 is the time, 06:00, not the temperature.)

items.q: At what time was the temperature 13 °C?
items.e: Find 13 on the scale (3 small squares above 10). Go across to the line and down: 16:00.

items.q: On the distance scale, what is each small square worth?
items.e: The labels go up in 200s. There are 2 small squares between two labels, so each square is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 m.

items.q: How far from home was Uju at 10:20?
items.e: At 10:20 the point is halfway between the lines for 600 and 700, so 650 m.

items.q: The park is the furthest point from home on Uju’s walk. How far from home is the park?
items.e: The highest part of the line is at 900 m (1 small square below 1,000). (1,800 m is there and back.)

items.q: Uju stopped at the park. When was she at the park?
items.e: When Uju stops, her distance from home does not change, so the line is flat. From 10:30 to 10:40 it stays at 900 m.

items.q: At 11:00 the line is back at 0 m. What does this mean?
items.e: The graph shows the distance from home. 0 m from home means Uju is at home again. She walked to the park and back.

items.q: How tall was the bean plant in week 2?
items.e: The labels go up in 10s and each small square is 2 cm. In week 2 the point is halfway between the lines for 10 and 12, so 11 cm.

items.q: In which week was the plant 24 cm tall?
items.e: Find 24 on the scale: 2 small squares above 20. Go across to the line and down: week 4.

items.q: How tall was the plant in week 5?
items.e: In week 5 the point is halfway between the lines for 28 and 30, so 29 cm.

items.q: In which week was the plant first taller than 20 cm?
items.e: In week 3 it was 18 cm, which is not taller than 20 cm. In week 4 it was 24 cm, so week 4 is the first.

items.q: How tall was the plant when it was first measured, in week 0?
items.e: Week 0 is the first point. It is halfway between the lines for 2 and 4, so 3 cm. (The plant was already 3 cm tall, not 0 cm.)

items.q: What was the temperature of the hot chocolate after 5 minutes?
items.e: The labels go up in 20s, so each small square is 10 °C. At 5 minutes the point is halfway between 60 and 70: 65 °C.

items.q: After how many minutes was the hot chocolate 40 °C?
items.e: Find 40 on the temperature scale, go across to the line, then down to the minutes: 20 minutes.

items.q: What was the temperature after 15 minutes?
items.e: At 15 minutes the point is halfway between 40 and 50, so 45 °C. (15 is the time, not the temperature.)

items.q: When was the hot chocolate cooling fastest?
items.e: Fastest means the steepest part of the line. From 0 to 5 minutes it fell 80 − 65 = 15 °C. In every other 5 minutes it fell 10 °C or less.

items.q: Between which two times did the temperature fall the most?
items.e: The line goes down after 14:00. 14:00 to 16:00: 18 − 13 = 5 °C. 16:00 to 18:00: 13 − 9 = 4 °C. So it fell most from 14:00 to 16:00. (10:00 to 12:00 is the biggest rise, not a fall.)

items.q: How many pupils in 5B have a packed lunch?
items.e: Find the Packed lunch row, then go across to the 5B column: 9. (11 is 5A.)

items.q: How many pupils in 5A have a school dinner?
items.e: School dinner row, 5A column: 14.

items.q: How many pupils are in 5A?
items.e: The Total row at the bottom gives each class. 5A: 14 + 11 + 3 = 28.

items.q: How many more pupils have a school dinner than a packed lunch?
items.e: Use the Total column. School dinner: 31. Packed lunch: 20. 31 − 20 = 11. (Using only one class gives 3 or 8.)

items.q: How many pupils are in Primary 5 altogether?
items.e: The bottom right cell is the total of everything: 28 + 30 = 58 pupils.

items.q: What time does the swimming pool close on Saturday?
items.e: Find the Saturday row, then go across to the Closes column: 17:30 (5:30 pm).

items.q: How long is the pool open on Sunday?
items.e: 09:30 to 15:30 is 6 hours. 15:30 to 16:00 is 30 minutes. So the pool is open 6 hours 30 minutes. (1,600 − 930 = 670 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: On which day is the pool open for the longest time?
items.e: Work out each day: Monday 13 hours 30 minutes, Wednesday 15 hours, Saturday 9 hours 30 minutes, Sunday 6 hours 30 minutes. Wednesday is the longest. (Monday opens just as early, but closes earlier.)

items.q: How many adult tickets were sold on Friday?
items.e: The adult row adds up to 183. Thursday is 86. 183 − 86 = 97 tickets. Check: 86 + 97 = 183.

items.q: How many child tickets were sold altogether?
items.e: Add along the Child row: 124 + 158 = 282. Remember to exchange: 4 + 8 = 12 units.

items.q: What number is missing from the table?
items.e: The bottom right cell is the total of all tickets. Add the Total column: 183 + 282 = 465. Check with the Total row: 210 + 255 = 465.

items.q: On which day were more child tickets sold, and how many more?
items.e: Child row: Thursday 124, Friday 158. Friday is more: 158 − 124 = 34.

items.q: How many boys cannot swim 25 m?
items.e: There are 45 boys. 38 of them can swim. 45 − 38 = 7 boys cannot.

items.q: How many pupils can swim 25 m?
items.e: Add down the Can column: 38 + 41 = 79. (92 is everyone in Primary 5, and 13 is the Cannot column.)

items.q: The bus leaves the Bus Station at 09:15. What time does it get to the Hospital?
items.e: Find 09:15 in the Bus Station row. Go down that column (Bus 2) to the Hospital row: 09:49.

items.q: Which bus does not stop at the Library?
items.e: A dash (—) means the bus does not stop there. The dash in the Library row is in the Bus 3 column.

items.q: How long does Bus 1 take from the Bus Station to the Retail Park?
items.e: 08:45 to 09:00 is 15 minutes. 09:00 to 09:32 is 32 minutes. 15 + 32 = 47 minutes. (87 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: How long does Bus 1 take from the High Street to the Library?
items.e: High Street 08:58, Library 09:06. 08:58 to 09:06 is 8 minutes.

items.q: Yusuf gets to the High Street at 09:31, just after a bus has left. How long must he wait for the next bus?
items.e: The bus at 09:28 has gone. The next bus at the High Street is at 09:58. From 09:31 to 09:58 is 27 minutes.

items.q: How long does it take to go from the High Street to the Hospital?
items.e: Use any bus that stops at both. Bus 2: High Street 09:28, Hospital 09:49. 09:28 to 09:49 is 21 minutes.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose football?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Football has 4 of them: 48 = 12.

items.q: Which sport was chosen by a quarter of the pupils?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Netball has 2 of them: 28 = 14.

items.q: Which colour was chosen by a quarter of the pupils?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Blue has 2 of them: 28 = 14.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose red?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Red has 3 of them: 38.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils walk to school?
items.e: The circle is split into 6 equal parts. Walk has 3 of them: 36 = 12.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils come by car?
items.e: The circle is split into 6 equal parts. Car has 2 of them: 26 = 13.

items.q: Which ways of travelling make half of the pie chart together?
items.e: Half of 6 parts is 3 parts. Car has 2 parts and Bus has 1 part: 2 + 1 = 3, so Car and Bus make 36 = 12.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils have a cat?
items.e: The circle is split into 12 equal parts. Cat has 3 of them: 312 = 14.

items.q: Which pet is 16 of the pie chart?
items.e: The circle is split into 12 equal parts. Fish has 2 of them: 212 = 16.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils did not choose blue?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Blue has 2 of them, so 8 − 2 = 6 parts are not Blue: 68 = 34.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose an apple or a pear?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Apple and Pear have 2 of them: 28 = 14.

items.q: Which fruit was chosen by half of the pupils?
items.e: The circle is split into 8 equal parts. Grapes has 4 of them: 48 = 12.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose spaghetti?
items.e: The circle is split into 10 equal parts. Spaghetti has 4 of them: 410 = 25.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils have a dog or a cat?
items.e: The circle is split into 12 equal parts. Dog and Cat have 9 of them: 912 = 34.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose egusi soup or pizza?
items.e: The circle is split into 10 equal parts. Egusi soup and Pizza have 5 of them: 510 = 12.

items.q: What fraction of the pupils chose spring?
items.e: The circle is split into 12 equal parts. Spring has 3 of them: 312 = 14.

items.q: How many pupils come by car?
items.e: Car is 2 of the 8 equal parts: 28 = 14 of the pie. 14 of 40 = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 pupils.

items.q: How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: Walk is half of the pie. Half of 40 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 pupils.

items.q: How many pupils cycle to school?
items.e: Bike is 1 of the 8 equal parts: 18 of 40 = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 pupils.

items.q: 200 pupils chose their favourite ice lolly. How many chose orange?
items.e: 10% of 200 = 200 ÷ 10 = 20. So 30% = 3 × 20 = 60 pupils. (30% is not 30 pupils: there are 200 pupils, not 100.)

items.q: All the angles in a pie chart add up to …
items.e: A pie chart is a whole circle, and the angles at the centre of a circle add up to 360°. (100 is for percentages.)

items.q: A pie chart shows 20 pupils. How many degrees stand for each pupil?
items.e: The whole circle is 360°. 360 ÷ 20 = 18°, so each pupil is 18°. (100 ÷ 20 = 5 uses 100, not 360.)

items.q: A pie chart shows 60 people. How many degrees stand for each person?
items.e: 360 ÷ 60 = 6, so each person is 6°.

items.q: 60 people were asked. 15 chose swimming. What angle should the swimming sector be?
items.e: Each person is 360 ÷ 60 = 6°. 15 × 6 = 90°. (Or: 15 out of 60 is 14, and 14 of 360° = 90°.)

items.q: 24 pupils were asked. 8 chose cricket. What angle should the cricket sector be?
items.e: Each pupil is 360 ÷ 24 = 15°. 8 × 15 = 120°. (Or: 8 out of 24 is 13, and 13 of 360° = 120°.)

items.q: 30 pupils were asked. 9 chose art. What angle should the art sector be?
A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 90°. What fraction of the pie chart is it?
items.e: Compare with the whole circle: 90360 = 14. (90100 uses 100, not 360.)

items.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 120°. What fraction of the pie chart is it?
items.e: 120360 = 13. Three sectors of 120° make 360°.

items.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 45°. What percentage of the pie chart is it?
items.e: 45360 = 18. 18 = 100% ÷ 8 = 12.5%.

items.q: A sector is 16 of a pie chart. What is its angle?
A sector is 25% of a pie chart. What is its angle?
items.e: 25% = 14. 360 ÷ 4 = 90°.

items.q: What is the angle of the Other sector?
What is the angle of the Swimming sector?
How many pupils chose football?
items.e: Each pupil is 360 ÷ 36 = 10°. 150 ÷ 10 = 15 pupils.

items.q: 45 pupils were asked. 18 chose football. What angle should the football sector be?
In a pie chart each pupil is 12°. The netball sector is 84°. How many pupils chose netball?
In a pie chart, a sector of 72° stands for 10 people. How many people does the whole pie chart show?
items.e: 72° × 5 = 360°, so the whole pie chart is 5 times as big as the sector: 5 × 10 = 50 people.

items.q: How many more pupils walk than come by car?
40 pupils were asked about pets: cat 10, dog 14, fish 6, other 10. What angle should the dog sector be?
How many pupils walk?
items.e: Each pupil is 360 ÷ 18 = 20°. 140 ÷ 20 = 7 pupils.
